title: gf2-algebra SIMD dispatch wiring + scalar fallback test
description:
Wire `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal3` to dispatch into the SIMD bipedal3 kernel (T12) at runtime, with a scalar fallback when AVX2 is absent, and add a forced-fallback test path.

## Background

T12 lands the SIMD primitive in `gf2-kernels-simd`. This issue wires the `gf2-algebra` permanent path to consume it: at runtime, `permanent_bipedal3` checks whether the SIMD backend is available (via the project's existing `OnceLock`-based detection) and dispatches accordingly. A `scalar_fallback` build flag forces the scalar path for testing on AVX2-capable hosts.

The crate-level `simd` feature controls compile-time inclusion of the kernel; runtime detection adds the per-CPU branch.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal3` consumes the SIMD bipedal3 kernel when the `simd` feature is on AND AVX2 is detected at runtime.
- [ ] [hard] Without the `simd` feature OR without AVX2, the function dispatches to the pure-Rust `permanent_bipedal3` (T9).
- [ ] [hard] A test forces the scalar fallback path (e.g., via a `#[cfg(test)]` knob on the dispatcher) and verifies output equality between SIMD and scalar at $n \in \{8, 16, 24, 32\}$: 100 random matrices each at $n \in \{8, 16, 24\}$ (fast tier or slow tier as needed) and at least 1 random matrix at $n = 32$ (slow tier, `#[ignore = "slow: ..."]`). The $n=32$ matrix count was reduced from the original 100 because a single permanent at $n=32$ takes ~6 s in release mode; 100 matrices would require ~600 s, far above the 120 s slow-tier limit. Amended 2026-05-11 to keep the contract testable.
- [ ] [hard] No regression in the existing T9/T11 test suites; correctness unchanged.
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes both with and without the `simd` feature.

## Amendment history (2026-05-11)

- Criterion 3 reduced the n=32 matrix count from 100 to ≥1. 100 matrices at n=32 at ~6 s each = ~600 s exceeds the 120 s slow-tier budget; the criterion's intent (force the SIMD vs scalar comparison at each n in the grid) is preserved with a smaller matrix count at the largest n.
